subjective.question: What is economic zoology?
subjective.answer: Economic Zoology is a sort of applied zoology, which involves the study of animals / living organisms that are of benefit or those that cause harm to humans.

subjective.question: Write tips for the safety of beekeepers.
subjective.answer: Bees can be dangerous, so a beekeeper must take several safety precautions when working around a honey bee colony: (1) A hat or veil is commonly used to keep the face and neck protected from stings. (2) Gloves are another popular form of beekeeping protection, although many beekeepers complain that gloves restrict their movement. (3) A hooded suit, typically made from a light coloured fabric to help distinguish the beekeeper from the honey bee's natural predators, may also be used. (4) A smoker is used to calm the bees: smoke masks the guard bees' alarm pheromones and encourages the other bees to feed by tricking them into thinking they will soon need to abandon their hive; it gives the beekeeper enough time to inspect the colony and perform any needed maintenance. Pine needles are used as fuel in the bee smoker.

subjective.question: What is an apiary?
subjective.answer: The place where a beekeeper keeps his bees is called an apiary or a bee yard.

subjective.question: What is apiculture?
subjective.answer: Apiculture is the technical term for beekeeping — beekeeping, especially on a commercial scale, for the sale of honey.

subjective.question: Differentiate between guard bees and soldier bees.
subjective.answer: Guard bees protect the entrance of the hive from enemies. Soldier bees hang around near the entrance and attack invaders; they work in concert with the entrance guards.

subjective.question: Differentiate between the queen bee and the drone bee.
subjective.answer: The Queen: the queen is the only sexually developed female in the hive; she is the largest bee in the colony; a productive queen can lay 2,000 eggs in a single day. The Drone: drones are stout male bees with large eyes and no stingers; they do not collect food or pollen from flowers; their sole purpose is to mate with the queen; they die upon mating; if the colony is short on food, drones are often kicked out of the hive.

subjective.question: Describe the reactions to a bee sting.
subjective.answer: Normal reaction: pain; a wheal (swelling) develops at the puncture site; redness develops around the wheal; swelling — a little at the site or a lot at the site (large local); itching. Allergic reaction: widespread, rapid swelling; itching of the body; a feeling of disorientation; stomach upset; loss of consciousness.

subjective.question: What is propolizing?
subjective.answer: The walls of the hive are covered with a thin coating of propolis, a resinous substance obtained from plants. In combination with enzymes added by the worker bees, it has antibacterial and antifungal properties. Propolis is also used to close off excessive ventilation and entrances.

subjective.question: What are the types of aquaculture systems?
subjective.answer: 1) Pond Fish Culture. 2) Raceway Culture. 3) Cage Fish Culture. 4) Recirculating Water Fish Culture.

subjective.question: What is the difference between intensive and extensive aquaculture?
subjective.answer: Extensive Aquaculture: minimal control, lower density — e.g. ponds; it is prevalent in third world countries. Intensive Aquaculture: highly controlled, high density — RAS, raceways, confined systems; e.g. in industrialized countries.

subjective.question: What is a raceway? (Marks: 2)
subjective.answer: Raceways are considered flow-through systems. Being simple to construct, they are some of the oldest designs in aquaculture. Water sources for raceway aquaculture operations are usually streams, springs, reservoirs or deep wells.

subjective.question: What is a hatchery?
subjective.answer: The eggs are incubated at the hatchery; they are kept warm until the chicks start to hatch out of their shells. Chickens hatch at around 20 days and turkeys hatch at around 27 days. Baby chickens are called chicks and baby turkeys are called poults.

subjective.question: What are the types of fish feeds?
subjective.answer: Finely ground meals; crumbles; flakes; pellets of various size and density — sinking, floating and slow sinking; and microdiet.

subjective.question: Write the advantages and disadvantages of the hand feeding method.
subjective.answer: In hand feeding, feed is distributed by hand, shovels or other non-automated means. It is the most common method and is used for feeds not suited to automated systems; meat scraps are hand fed. Advantages: (1) the operator can note feeding behaviour and gauge the feed required; (2) the operator can ensure that feed is dispersed over a wide area. Disadvantages: (1) high labour cost; (2) increased handling of the feed.

subjective.question: Differentiate between demand feeders and auger feeding.
subjective.answer: Demand feeders allow fish to bump a rod and release feed when they are hungry; they are used in raceways and the fish must be trained how to use them — fish can obtain food on demand by depressing a trigger. Auger feeding is similar to the systems used by swine and poultry farmers: feed is stored in large tanks and moved by augers that drop feed into the pond; it is common in tanks and raceways.

subjective.question: What are the protein requirements of fish? (Marks: 3)
subjective.answer: Fish contain 60–93% crude protein, thus fish diets are higher in protein than those of birds and animals. Fish appear to be relatively efficient utilizers of protein to energy, with 84% efficiency. Fish cannot synthesize their amino acids and obtain them chiefly from the diet; their absence affects the growth of fish.

subjective.question: What are the factors affecting the protein requirements of fish?
subjective.answer: Protein requirements are affected by limited digestion: about 36% of feed is excreted as organic waste, because a large fraction of the feed remains undigested and is excreted. Live fish biomass produces about 5 times more waste than humans.

subjective.question: What are the mineral requirements of fish?
subjective.answer: Fish have the ability to absorb a number of minerals directly from water, reducing the mineral requirements in the diet. Fish require all the macro- and micro-elements required by other animals, for enzymes and cofactors. Fish in soft water (low mineral content) require additional supplements in the diet.

subjective.question: What are the functions of fat?
subjective.answer: 1) Providing energy. 2) Cushions for vital organs. 3) Energy reserves. 4) Insulators and lubricants. 5) Transport of fat-soluble vitamins.

subjective.question: Define fat.
subjective.answer: Fat consists of fat-soluble compounds occurring in plant and animal tissues — fats, phospholipids, sterols, fatty acids etc. Excessive dietary lipid causes nutritional disease, e.g. fatty liver or visceral fat. Fish can utilize the energy of fat with 84% efficiency.

subjective.question: Name the fat-soluble vitamins.
subjective.answer: The fat-soluble vitamins are Vitamin A, Vitamin D, Vitamin E and Vitamin K.

subjective.question: How do we determine (test) water quality?
subjective.answer: The water quality parameters often tested are: (a) Dissolved oxygen, (b) Water temperature, (c) pH, (d) Total Ammonia Nitrogen, (e) Nitrite/Nitrate, (f) Alkalinity/Hardness, (g) Salinity.

subjective.question: Define oligotrophic and eutrophic systems.
subjective.answer: Oligotrophic: excellent water quality; very clear; used in display aquaria; most frequently used for breeding purposes; some species are kept in these conditions all of their lives, while others for a period of time. Eutrophic: these exist for the grow-out of the most tolerant species that show vigorous growth under moderately deteriorated water quality conditions — dissolved oxygen at the economic optimum level, ammonia and nitrite less than 2 mg-N/L, and marginal water quality. Species evolved under similar natural conditions prosper in these conditions.

subjective.question: What is mesotrophic?
subjective.answer: Mesotrophic describes the bulk of high-density production systems where risk and economics must be carefully balanced to achieve profitability.

subjective.question: Write about aeration and oxygenation in recirculating fish culture.
subjective.answer: Oxygen is the first limiting factor in a recirculation fish culture system; O2 is consumed by the fish and by the bacteria inhabiting the biofilter. In the fish tank, O2 should not be less than 5 ppm, and in the outgoing biofilter water not less than 2 ppm. When these levels drop below these concentrations, aeration becomes necessary. Induction of air into water is called aeration, while induction of pure oxygen is called oxygenation. For stocking densities up to 45 kg/m³ aeration is enough, but for higher stocking densities oxygenation is a must.

subjective.question: What are the features and applications of the effluent (recirculation) tank system?
subjective.answer: Features: high concentrations of suspended and dissolved solids; high ammonia levels and high concentration of CO2; low levels of dissolved oxygen; application of a recirculation system. Applications: brood stock maturation; nursing and larval rearing systems; nutrition and health research systems; short-term holding systems; ornamental and display tanks; high density grow-out of food fish.

subjective.question: Name the commonly cultured fish species with their scientific names. (Marks: 5)
subjective.answer: Rohu — Labeo rohita; Morakhi — Cirrhinus mrigala; Catla/Thaila — Catla catla; Grass carp — Ctenopharyngodon idella; Silver carp — Hypophthalmichthys molitrix; Big head carp — Aristichthys nobilis; Common carp — Cyprinus carpio; Tilapia — Oreochromis niloticus.

subjective.question: Name some aquaculture journals.
subjective.answer: Journal of the World Aquaculture Society; North American Journal of Aquaculture (PFC); Aquaculture; Journal of Applied Aquaculture; Aquaculture Nutrition; Aquaculture Research; Journal of Aquatic Animal Health; Transactions of the American Fisheries Society.

subjective.question: What is fish health and why is it important?
subjective.answer: Health or well-being of fish is important for feeding, growth and reproduction. Diseased fish results in poor growth and ends up in losses; further, when diseased fish is sent to the consumer, it changes in texture, appearance and taste.

subjective.question: What are the causes of fish disease?
subjective.answer: Bad water quality; inappropriate diet; temperature (too high or too low); stress; bullying (mistreatment, oppression); viral diseases; fungal infections; bacterial infections; and parasites.

subjective.question: What is a parasite?
subjective.answer: A parasite is an organism that lives off another, often to the detriment of the host's health. Parasites can be internal (endo-parasites) or external (ecto-parasites). They can be protozoan (single celled), nematodes / cestodes / trematodes (worms), or crustacean (e.g. louse).

subjective.question: What are bacteria?
subjective.answer: Bacteria are microscopic single-celled organisms that can reproduce rapidly. They are naturally present in aquarium water, e.g. Pseudomonas fluorescens.

subjective.question: What is a virus?
subjective.answer: A virus is a microscopic organism that can only reproduce by inhabiting host cells and using the genetic material in the cells of a host.

subjective.question: Define fungus. (Marks: 2)
subjective.answer: Fungi are multi-cellular, spore-producing organisms that live off other organisms and dead matter; some are parasitic. Fungal spores are commonly found in aquarium water.

subjective.question: Write the cause, symptoms and treatment of Spring Viremia of Carp.
subjective.answer: Cause: a viral infection caused by Rhabdovirus carpio. Symptoms: darkening of skin, pale gills, pop eye, protruding vent, bleeding in gills, skin and eyes; lethargy, abnormal swimming positions, sitting on the bottom of the tank. Treatment: no known treatment.

subjective.question: What is whirling disease?
subjective.answer: Whirling disease is caused by the protozoan Myxobolus cerebralis, which causes skull deformation in fish.

subjective.question: Write the causes and symptoms of white spot disease (ich).
subjective.answer: Causes: a protozoan parasite, either free swimming in the water or carried in with new fish or plants; fish under stress from bad water conditions are more susceptible. Symptoms: the fish's skin and fins are covered in tiny white spots; a badly affected fish may make rapid gill movements.

subjective.question: Write the characteristics of Bombyx mori.
subjective.answer: It cannot fly; its caterpillars have no real locomotion; the female is larger than the male; the male has big plumose antennae.

subjective.question: What is lac?
subjective.answer: Lac is the only known commercial resin of animal origin. It is the hardened resin secreted by tiny lac insects belonging to a bug family. To produce 1 kg of lac resin, around 300,000 insects lose their life. The lac insect yields resin, lac dye and lac wax.

subjective.question: Write the composition of lac.
subjective.answer: Lac is a mixture of several substances, of which resin is the main constituent. The approximate percentages are: Resin — 68 to 90%; Dye — 2 to 10%; Wax — 5 to 6%; Mineral matter — 3 to 7%; Albuminous matter — 5 to 10%; Water — 2 to 3%.

subjective.question: What is the technique of lac culture? (Marks: 3)
subjective.answer: Lac is a natural resin of animal origin. It is secreted by an insect known as the lac insect; in order to obtain lac, these insects are cultured, and the technique is called lac-culture.

subjective.question: Write the stages (life cycle) of the lac insect.
subjective.answer: The life cycle of the lac insect takes about six months and consists of the stages: 1) Egg, 2) Nymph, 3) Instars, 4) Pupa, 5) Adult.

subjective.question: Define swarming. (Marks: 2)
subjective.answer: Lac larvae begin to wander in search of a suitable place to fix themselves. This mass movement of larvae from the female cell to the new off-shoots of the host plant is termed swarming. Swarming occurs after the emergence of the nymph and it may continue for 5 weeks.

subjective.question: Differentiate between natural and artificial infection in lac culture.
subjective.answer: Natural infection: when infection from one plant to another occurs by the natural movements of the insect, it is called natural infection; this may be due to overcrowding of the insect population and non-availability of tender shoots on a particular tree. Artificial infection: it takes place through agencies other than those of nature; prior to about two weeks of hatching, lac-bearing sticks are cut to the size of six inches — they are called brood lac.

subjective.question: What is inoculation?
subjective.answer: The method by which the lac insects are introduced to the new lac host plant is known as inoculation.

subjective.question: Differentiate between Ari lac and Phunki lac.
subjective.answer: Lac can be scraped from the twigs before or after the emergence of larvae. If it is used for manufacturing before the emergence of larvae, the type of lac produced is called Ari lac; and if it is used for manufacturing purposes after the swarming of larvae has occurred, the lac is said to be Phunki lac.

subjective.question: Write the uses of lac.
subjective.answer: Lac has been used for the welfare of human beings since olden days; although synthetic products have reduced its importance a little, it is still included in the list of necessary articles. Lac is used in making toys, bracelets, sealing wax and gramophone records. It is also used in making grinding stones, for filling ornaments, for manufacturing varnishes and paints, for silvering the back of mirrors, and for encasing cable wires. Waste material produced during the processing of stick lac is used for dyeing purposes; nail polish is a good example of a by-product of lac.

subjective.question: Write the importance of lac.
subjective.answer: With increasing universal environmental awareness, the importance of lac has assumed special relevance in the present age, being (a) eco-friendly, (b) biodegradable and (c) a self-sustaining natural material. Since lac insects are cultured on host trees growing primarily in wasteland areas, promotion of lac and its culture can help in eco-system development as well as reasonably high economic returns. It is a source of livelihood for the tribal and poor people inhabiting forest and sub-forest areas.

subjective.question: Define pullet. (Marks: 2)
subjective.answer: A pullet is a young, immature female chicken less than 5–6 months of age.

subjective.question: What is plumage?
subjective.answer: Plumage is the feathers of a bird.

subjective.question: What is a broiler?
subjective.answer: Chickens grown for meat production are called broilers.

subjective.question: How is the abdominal capacity of a hen measured and expressed?
subjective.answer: The abdominal capacity of a hen is measured and expressed by one's fingers width. The normal capacity is 3 fingers width by 4 fingers width.

subjective.question: Define catching in poultry.
subjective.answer: Once the birds reach their required weight, they are transported to the processing plant. Trained staff called catchers catch the birds and put them in special containers called modules. Catching is carried out quietly and with care, to avoid unnecessary stress and to prevent injury to the birds.
